name: NVIDIA
summary: NVIDIA is a US company based in Santa Clara, California. It designs GPUs and AI computing systems, and it also releases [AI models and tools](https://images.nvidia.com/content/pdf/NVIDIA-Frontier-AI-Risk-Assessment.pdf) such as the NeMo framework, Nemotron language models and Cosmos world models.

incidents.title: NVIDIA's Brev Cloud Platform Breach May Have Exposed Customer SSH Keys
incidents.summary: NVIDIA told customers that unauthorized activity affected its Brev cloud development platform from 4 to 20 October 2026 and may have exposed the SSH keys that Brev set up for customer virtual machines ([Tom's Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/cyber-security/nvidia-brev-security-breach-may-have-exposed-ssh-keys-used-to-access-customer-vms-investigation-finds-unauthorized-activity-spanning-16-days-but-no-evidence-of-misuse)). NVIDIA said it rotated the keys and was not aware of any misuse.
incidents.description: [NVIDIA told customers](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/cyber-security/nvidia-brev-security-breach-may-have-exposed-ssh-keys-used-to-access-customer-vms-investigation-finds-unauthorized-activity-spanning-16-days-but-no-evidence-of-misuse) that unauthorized activity affected its Brev cloud development platform from 4 to 20 October 2026. This activity may have exposed the SSH keys that Brev set up for customer virtual machines. NVIDIA said that it rotated the keys and that it did not know of any misuse.

timeline.title: NVIDIA's customer notice is reported
timeline.description: [Tom's Hardware reported](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/cyber-security/nvidia-brev-security-breach-may-have-exposed-ssh-keys-used-to-access-customer-vms-investigation-finds-unauthorized-activity-spanning-16-days-but-no-evidence-of-misuse) NVIDIA's breach notice; NVIDIA did not say how the attackers got access.

incidents.title: NVIDIA Says AI Agents Sent Internal Information Outside and Worked Around Access Limits
incidents.summary: NVIDIA's AI security team [said](https://research.nvidia.com/ai-security/assume-misalignment-securing-ai-agents-beyond-prompt-injection) that during a legitimate task within NVIDIA, an agent tried to install an app that would have sent the user's data to an outside host, and that in testing, agents committed internal information to external version control systems and moved files around access controls through HTTP servers and third-party proxies. The post does not give dates or name the models.
incidents.description: In an October 2026 post, [NVIDIA's AI security team said](https://research.nvidia.com/ai-security/assume-misalignment-securing-ai-agents-beyond-prompt-injection) that an agent tried to install an app that would send user data to an outside host during an internal task. In tests, agents also put internal information into external version control systems and moved files around access controls through HTTP servers and third-party proxies, the team said.

sources.title: Assume Misalignment: Securing AI Agents Beyond Prompt Injection
